notes: Template battle_owner_15.c (Item_CanOwnerEquipDirect-shaped: two early-return checks then a single ability-flag test) gave the right M2C_FIELD idiom and general shape, but this owner's actual control flow (from games/gs1/asm/080a46b4.s) is a materially extended variant: masked = itemId & 0x1ff; two calls (Func_08077018 for item data, then Func_0808a490(masked) which short-circuits to `return 0` if nonzero); Func_08077080 is called UNCONDITIONALLY on (field40 & 0x3fff) to get an ability pointer even before the field40!=0 guard is checked (field40 is read from memory twice: once for the call argument, once for the guard, rather than being cached); nested field2/field12 checks decide whether Func_08077218(owner, masked) gets consulted; and the final ability-flag check is a 3-way result (2 / 1 / 0 / -1) driven by bits 0x40 and 0x80 of ability byte 1 and a `field8==0xff` check, not the template's simple 2-vs-0 test.

Iterated 4 respellings, converging from wrong_instructions=42 down to 16 (candidate 156B vs reference 160B, a 4-byte/2-instruction residual). Key fixes: (a) splitting `masked = itemId & 0x1ff` into a plain-copy-then-AND-in-place (two statements) instead of one combined-expression AND, matching the reference's adds-then-ands register reuse; (b) moving the Func_08077080 call to read field40 fresh via M2C_FIELD directly as its argument (not through a cached local), and reading field40 AGAIN via M2C_FIELD for the `!= 0` guard immediately after the call, instead of guarding before the call and reusing one cached value; (c) restructuring the field2/field12/Func_08077218 logic as three explicit nested `if` statements (matching reference's branch order exactly: field40 guard, then field2, then field12, then the call) rather than an if/else-if with a compound `&&` condition.

Residual: the final `(field1 & 0x80) ? -1 : 0` bit test compiles to a single `lsrs r3,r2,#7` (extract bit 7 directly) in the candidate, versus the reference's `movs r3,#128; ands r3,r2` (explicit mask-and) -- both are followed by the identical branchless negate/or/lsrs-#31 sign-extraction tail (which matches exactly), so this is purely which of two equal-cost single-bit-test encodings the compiler picks. Tried the same test as an explicit `!= 0` comparison, as a bare truthy ternary, and with the loaded byte declared `s8` instead of `u8` (this last one regressed the match to wrong_instructions=28, so reverted) -- none produced the AND form. The identical bit-test earlier in the same function (`field1 & 0x40`, used as a genuine branch condition rather than a value fed into a branchless ternary) DOES compile to the AND form in both candidate and reference, suggesting the shift-vs-mask choice is driven by whether the bit test result flows into a conditional branch or into a value-producing expression -- a compiler-internal codegen choice I could not reach by respelling the C, not a remaining logic/shape gap.

This 2-instruction residual is the only remaining difference; a permuter-style search over just that one sub-expression's phrasing (rather than further manual guessing) is the most promising next step.

measured=2026-08-29 (resolved): the missing piece was register-pressure/pseudo-materialization timing, not the ternary's phrasing. Hoisting `s32 mask = 0x80;` immediately before the ternary (same block as the `else`) still produced `lsrs`. But declaring `s32 mask = 0x80;` at the TOP of the `if (result == 1) { ... }` block -- i.e. before `u8 field1 = M2C_FIELD(abilityData, u8, 1);` and thus before the `field1 & 0x40` branch that comes first -- makes GCC 2.96 materialize 0x80 into its own register early, and it then reuses that register for the final bit test as `movs r3,#128` / `ands r3,r2`, matching the reference exactly. Final form: `if (result == 1) { s32 mask = 0x80; u8 field1 = ...; if ((field1 & 0x40) != 0) {...} else { result = (field1 & mask) ? -1 : 0; } }`.
